records.spacelift: One GraphQL endpoint with 285 queries and 380 mutations ([report 02](../research/reference/02-graphql-to-rest-mapping.md))
records.infraweave: REST over JSON described by OpenAPI 3 (`api/deploy.openapi.yaml`); no GraphQL endpoint and no GraphQL facade. The reference spec projects every root field to a route, and the served spec is scaffolded from it family by family
records.why: Standard HTTP status codes, caching, per-route authorization and rate limits; the chi and oapi-codegen toolchain; Spacelift's clients use fixed selections, so GraphQL's client-shaped queries buy nothing
records.impact: spacectl, `terraform-provider-spacelift`, the Bruno collection and direct GraphQL callers cannot talk to infraweave; a port changes transport, paths and bodies. Migration from Spacelift is a data import

records.spacelift: spacectl and `terraform-provider-spacelift` are the clients
records.infraweave: infraweave's own clients: the provider (`weaveplatform/terraform-provider-infraweave`) and `infraweavectl`, both built on the SDK, `pkg/sdk`, and checked against Spacelift's provider schema and spacectl's command list ([0016](../research/decisions/0016-testing-and-acceptance.md#the-terraform-provider-parity-oracle))
records.why: Follows from DV-001; a client that speaks GraphQL cannot reach a REST server
records.impact: Terraform configurations change provider source and any renamed attributes recorded in `api/reference/provider-parity.yaml`; scripts move from `spacectl` to `infraweavectl`

records.spacelift: No retry-safety mechanism for mutations; a create that times out cannot be retried without risking a duplicate
records.infraweave: `POST` and `PATCH` accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 characters), scoped to the caller and kept 24 hours by default. A finished request with the same fingerprint replays with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; a different fingerprint answers `422` `idempotency-key-reuse`; one in flight answers `409` `idempotency-key-in-flight`
records.why: Terraform providers and CI scripts retry on network errors; only the client knows whether two requests are one intent
records.impact: None for a client that sends no key; a retrying client opts in by sending one

records.spacelift: No published load contract per caller
records.infraweave: One token bucket per caller per cost class, `standard` or `expensive`, named per operation in `x-infraweave-cost`. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; an empty bucket answers `429` `rate-limited` with `Retry-After`
records.why: Searches, batches and run triggers cost far more than reads; a visible budget lets clients slow down before they are throttled
records.impact: Clients honour `429` and `Retry-After`; fan-out callers see the smaller `expensive` budget

records.spacelift: No per-caller API switch for the operator
records.infraweave: The operator can disable the API for one caller, who receives `503` `api-disabled` with `Retry-After`; other callers are unaffected
records.why: Shedding one misbehaving caller without shedding everyone
records.impact: None unless the operator disables the caller

records.spacelift: 95 list fields return bare arrays, such as `GET /stacks` in the reference
records.infraweave: Every list `GET` takes `limit` (default 20, maximum 100, clamped) and an opaque `cursor`, and returns a `<Type>Page` with `items` and `nextCursor`, present only when another page exists; no total count. Cursors are keyset positions that never expire; a bad one answers `400` `invalid-cursor`. `POST .../search` keeps relay-style `first`, `after` and `pageInfo`
records.why: Unbounded lists load everything at once; offset paging is O(n) and unstable under writes
records.impact: A port pages until `nextCursor` is absent instead of reading one array

records.spacelift: Error identity is message text in GraphQL `errors`
records.infraweave: Each problem `type` is a URN, `urn:infraweave:problem:<slug>`, from one registry of slugs (0003's five, extended by DV-084)
records.why: RFC 9457 lets clients match on `type` without dereferencing it, and infraweave has no documentation host to resolve a URL to
records.impact: Clients branch on the `type` slug; see DV-084 for the text kept for ported clients

records.spacelift: Ships the launcher as a separate binary and image that embeds the worker binary ([report 10](../research/reference/10-workers-and-execution.md))
records.infraweave: The launcher is the `launcher` process mode of the one `infraweave` binary, and the runner inside the run container is the hidden `runner` subcommand of the same static binary, which the launcher mounts
records.why: Launcher, runner and server share a version by construction; the launcher's package graph stays free of server code, so `cmd/infraweave-agent`, a build for worker hosts that links only `internal/agent`, is a one-file change when image size or a review requires it
records.impact: Worker hosts run `infraweave launcher` in place of Spacelift's launcher image; custom runner images need no embedded worker binary

records.spacelift: Self-hosted supports PostgreSQL 14 to 18 ([report 24](../research/reference/24-self-hosted-reference.md))
records.infraweave: The floor is the newest major that Amazon RDS, Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server and Cloud SQL all offer, PostgreSQL 18 at the baseline; it rises in the first release after all three offer the next major
records.why: Every reference deployment can create a database at the floor, and CI gates on one major while the next runs beside it
records.impact: An operator on PostgreSQL 14 to 17 upgrades before installing

records.spacelift: Self-hosted provisions one bucket per purpose
records.infraweave: One bucket with a prefix per store by default; a per-store override keeps separate buckets where policy requires them
records.why: Eleven buckets are eleven pieces of infrastructure to provision before a first run
records.impact: Operators may provision one bucket; existing per-purpose buckets map through the override

records.spacelift: Relies on bucket lifecycle rules for expiry and asks for bucket versioning on the states bucket
records.infraweave: infraweave writes every object under an immutable key, records it in `blob_objects`, and expires and versions objects itself; state history needs no bucket versioning. A lifecycle rule is at most an operator backstop set longer than the store's retention
records.why: Retention and state history become database facts the API can list and test; the local-disk driver and minimal S3-compatible stores need neither feature
records.impact: Operators drop versioning and lifecycle requirements from the bucket; tooling that read old state versions from bucket versions reads them through the API

records.spacelift: The in-run API token's issuer is Spacelift's
records.infraweave: `iss` defaults to the public URL and is configurable; the other claim formats match Spacelift's by default, with configurable templates
records.why: The in-run token's issuer is infraweave's public URL like every other infraweave token, and an operator can change it
records.impact: None for the provider, which reads `sub`; code that checks `iss` sees the installation's URL

pending.settles: The in-run token `sub`, external ID suffixes, `RoleSessionName` and the federation algorithm

records.spacelift: `ApiKeyInput.admin`, a required `Boolean!`, makes an admin key; the changelog deprecates it and the schema does not ([report 14](../research/reference/14-spaces-rbac-and-identity.md#81-types-and-fields))
records.infraweave: The field is not accepted: a body that sets it answers `400` `invalid-request` like any unknown field. A key becomes an administrator through a `space-admin` role binding on the account's top space, and the key's `admin` reads whether that binding exists
records.why: One source of truth for access; decision 0021 treats the changelog-deprecated field as superseded
records.impact: A port drops the field, which Spacelift's provider always sends as `false`, and binds the key to `space-admin` on the account's top space instead

records.spacelift: Fetches OIDC API key issuers as configured
records.infraweave: Issuers are fetched over HTTPS only, optionally restricted to `auth.oidc_api_keys.allowed_issuers`
records.why: A self-hosted server fetching user-supplied URLs is an SSRF path
records.impact: OIDC API keys whose issuer is plain HTTP, or outside a configured allowlist, are refused

records.spacelift: Self-hosted documents no rotation of its JWT signing key ([report 24](../research/reference/24-self-hosted-reference.md#35-encryption-and-kms))
records.infraweave: Signing keys rotate automatically every 90 days
records.why: Rotation limits key exposure
records.impact: Relying parties read the JWKS document rather than pinning one key

records.spacelift: Does not document reissue of the federation token during a run ([report 12](../research/reference/12-cloud-integrations-and-oidc.md))
records.infraweave: The federation token file is refreshed during long runs
records.why: A run past one hour otherwise loses cloud access
records.impact: None; runs longer than the token lifetime keep their cloud credentials

records.spacelift: Browser session lifetime is undocumented
records.infraweave: Session lifetimes are stated, configurable defaults
records.why: A self-hosted operator needs a known value
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: Seat limits by plan
records.infraweave: Seats are the `seats` limit of the organization's tier, pooled across its accounts, counting each member once and API keys as Spacelift counts them, and enforced only while billing is on (DV-101); a seat beyond the pool, or beyond an account limit an organization admin sets, answers `403` `limit-reached`
records.why: Seats are one more tier limit, with one refusal for every limit
records.impact: None while billing is off; with billing on, the limits of Spacelift's documented plans until the operator changes them

records.spacelift: The `legacy` space carries access-policy behaviour
records.infraweave: `legacy` is an ordinary space with no special semantics
records.why: Access policies, its only special behaviour, are superseded
records.impact: None for clients; imported access policies follow the supersession register

records.spacelift: System role contents are not published ([report 14](../research/reference/14-spaces-rbac-and-identity.md))
records.infraweave: System role contents are derived from the legacy fallback column of the action catalogue; parity is checked against `Role.actions` once captured
records.why: A role either grants an action or the fallback level decides, as one set-membership test
records.impact: A system role's action list may differ from Spacelift's until the capture lands

records.spacelift: The worker pool controller and drift detection system roles' slugs are unrecorded
records.infraweave: Their slugs are `worker-pool-controller` and `drift-detection-manager`
records.why: A slug is needed to bind them
records.impact: Configurations that name Spacelift's slugs for these roles may need the name changed

records.spacelift: The schema marks some actions "do not use"
records.infraweave: Disabled actions cannot be assigned to roles; operations they would govern use their fallback
records.why: A role must not depend on an action that grants nothing
records.impact: A role create or update naming a disabled action is rejected

records.spacelift: Two statements conflict on whether an `ACTIVE` managed user with no binding can log in
records.infraweave: Such a user logs in with empty grants
records.why: The newer changelog statement wins
records.impact: None

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: Workers talk MQTT or HTTP long-poll; self-hosted runs a built-in broker or bridges to IoT Core, and keeps an `iot` queue for worker messages
records.infraweave: HTTP long-poll only, under `/worker/v1`; no MQTT transport, broker listener or IoT Core bridge, and no `iot` queue
records.why: Spacelift retires MQTT for workers on 2027-03-30; a broker adds a port, a component and a second delivery path; Spacelift's launchers cannot reach infraweave anyway (DV-001)
records.impact: Worker networks need outbound HTTPS to `serve` only; load balancer idle timeouts must exceed the poll hold by 15 seconds

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: Leaves a run alone while a worker executes it, for up to 30 days
records.infraweave: A run whose worker stays offline for `run.lost_after` (default 60 minutes) is a lost run: it fails with note `worker lost` and releases the stack. A worker that returns in time lets its run continue
records.why: A stack should not stay locked for weeks behind a dead host, and an hour rides out restarts and short outages without killing a half-applied run
records.impact: A run on a crashed worker fails after an hour and can then be retried, instead of holding the stack

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: Defaults to Spacelift's own runner images
records.infraweave: Defaults to infraweave's own runner images; the shared image contract (UID 1983, the same configuration precedence) keeps Spacelift's images usable
records.why: An installation does not depend on another vendor's registry
records.impact: None for stacks that name an image; stacks on the default get infraweave's

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: Launcher settings are `SPACELIFT_*` environment variables
records.infraweave: Launcher settings are named `INFRAWEAVE_LAUNCHER_*`
records.why: The launcher is infraweave's client, not Spacelift's
records.impact: Worker deployment configuration renames its variables

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: `REGO_V0` is the provider's default engine; the API's default is unverified
records.infraweave: `REGO_V1` is the default when a create omits the engine
records.why: Rego v1 is OPA's current language
records.impact: A policy written for v0 sets the engine explicitly

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: Removes `http.send`, `opa.runtime`, `rego.parse_module`, `time.now_ns` and `trace` from policies
records.infraweave: Also removes `net.lookup_ip_addr`
records.why: DNS lookups from the server reach the network the other removals keep policies away from
records.impact: A policy using `net.lookup_ip_addr` fails to compile at save

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: Documents no outcome for a policy evaluation error
records.infraweave: Each policy type has a stated fail-closed outcome; an `APPROVAL` error leaves the run waiting
records.why: A policy that cannot be evaluated must not let a plan apply or a user log in
records.impact: None for policies that evaluate; a broken policy blocks rather than passes

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: The `sanitized` helper's truncation of SHA-256 is unverified ([report 20](../research/reference/20-vendors.md#13-resource-sanitization))
records.infraweave: `sanitized` uses infraweave's own truncation
records.why: A rule is needed until a capture shows Spacelift's
records.impact: A policy comparing sanitized values with strings produced by Spacelift may not match

records.spacelift: External state access uses the Terraform `remote` backend
records.infraweave: External access uses the Terraform `http` backend with a token
records.why: The `remote` API is a second surface with its own JSON:API shapes and login flow; `http` already serves `terraform_remote_state` and `terraform state pull`
records.impact: Configurations that read state from outside change to `backend "http"`

records.spacelift: State upload and download URLs point at the object store
records.infraweave: They point at infraweave, which proxies and keeps state sealed at rest
records.why: The server holds the encryption; states are small enough to proxy
records.impact: Worker networks need no route to the bucket for state

records.spacelift: The lock kind taken while planning is undocumented
records.infraweave: Planning takes a shared lock
records.why: Concurrent read-only plans need not serialise
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: A stopped run can leave a state lock behind
records.infraweave: A run's locks are released when it ends
records.why: No stuck lock needs a manual unlock
records.impact: None; manual unlock is rarely needed

records.spacelift: SaaS keeps non-current state versions for 30 days
records.infraweave: Non-current versions are kept 90 days by default (`state.noncurrent_retention`; `0` keeps them forever)
records.why: Long enough to roll back past a quarter's changes, while storage stays bounded
records.impact: Rollback reaches further back than on SaaS; an operator may shorten or lengthen it

records.spacelift: Self-hosted offers SQS or a PostgreSQL queue
records.infraweave: The PostgreSQL queue only
records.why: Enqueue joins the change's transaction, which SQS cannot
records.impact: Operators provision no SQS queues

records.spacelift: A fixed receive count of 3 before dead-lettering
records.infraweave: A retry limit per job kind, default 5, with exponential backoff and full jitter
records.why: Different kinds tolerate different numbers of failures
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: Separate dead-letter queues
records.infraweave: A `dead` job state kept 30 days, listed and acted on through three operations of the operator API, outside the Spacelift surface: `GET /operator/v1/queue/jobs`, `POST /operator/v1/queue/jobs/{id}/retry`, `DELETE /operator/v1/queue/jobs/{id}`
records.why: Dead work is inspectable and retryable in place
records.impact: New operator API; no Spacelift client uses it

records.spacelift: A separate FIFO queue
records.infraweave: Ordering keys on jobs
records.why: Ordering applies per key, not per queue
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: SaaS installs Spacelift's GitHub Marketplace app
records.infraweave: The operator registers a GitHub App, as self-hosted Spacelift requires
records.why: infraweave has no global app of its own
records.impact: Operators create and register an app; repositories install that app

records.spacelift: Spacelift's own webhook endpoints
records.infraweave: Webhook URLs under `/webhooks/vcs/`
records.why: One route family for every provider
records.impact: VCS webhook configurations point at the new path

records.spacelift: One webhook secret at a time
records.infraweave: The previous secret is accepted for a window after rotation
records.why: Rotation without dropped deliveries
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: No delivery listing or replay
records.infraweave: Routes to list received deliveries and replay one
records.why: Debugging a missed trigger without the provider's console
records.impact: New operations; no Spacelift client uses them

records.spacelift: VCS agents speak gRPC to a separate gateway service with its own load balancer
records.infraweave: `infraweave vcs-agent` long-polls `serve` over HTTPS with its own token layout; no gateway process and no gRPC listener
records.why: Reuses the worker protocol's shape and any HTTPS load balancer
records.impact: `spacelift-vcs-agent` does not connect; agent pools run `infraweave vcs-agent`

records.spacelift: The docs promise a strict request allowlist; the released agent at the research pin validates nothing
records.infraweave: The allowlist is on by default, derived from the client's own route table, and the agent refuses unmatched Azure DevOps requests
records.why: Without validation the agent is a general proxy into a private network
records.impact: Integrations that relied on unvalidated proxying fail until their route is listed

pending.settles: Whether the released VCS agent validates requests, which decides whether this departs from the agent as well as from the docs

records.spacelift: The individual commit check name is undocumented
records.infraweave: `infraweave/<stack slug>`
records.why: A stable name is needed for branch protection
records.impact: Branch protection rules copied from Spacelift need the check name changed

records.spacelift: The choice between KMS and an RSA key is permanent; only KMS keys rotate, yearly
records.infraweave: `infraweave secrets rewrap` moves the keyring between a local key, KMS providers or a new key in a few statements
records.why: Operators change custody without a reinstall
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: Kubernetes deployments can use only RSA
records.infraweave: GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and Vault are offered beside AWS KMS
records.why: Every reference deployment gets a managed key option
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: In the local-key mode one RSA key both encrypts and signs
records.infraweave: The JWT signing key is a separate sealed row, apart from the encryption root
records.why: Rotating one never touches the other
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: Documents no minimum length for masked values
records.infraweave: Values shorter than 4 bytes are not masked in run logs
records.why: Masking `1` or `on` destroys the log and protects nothing
records.impact: A secret shorter than 4 bytes appears in logs; such secrets should be lengthened

records.spacelift: Splits registry discovery (`spacelift.io`) from the protocol host (`app.spacelift.io`)
records.infraweave: Discovery and the protocol share the installation's host
records.why: One host to deploy, certify and allow
records.impact: Module and provider source addresses use the installation host

records.spacelift: A failed provider verification blocks neither publishing nor use
records.infraweave: Publishing a provider version checks that every uploaded file exists and matches its declared checksum
records.why: A bad upload fails at publish, not at `terraform init`
records.impact: Publishing pipelines see an error for a bad upload

records.spacelift: Labels registry protocol 404 bodies `text/plain`
records.infraweave: Serves them as `application/json`
records.why: The body is JSON
records.impact: None for Terraform and OpenTofu

records.spacelift: Behaviour for yanked versions is uncaptured
records.infraweave: Yanked versions are neither listed nor downloadable, even by an exact pin
records.why: A yanked version is withdrawn
records.impact: An exact pin to a yanked version fails to install

pending.settles: What Spacelift does with yanked versions

records.spacelift: Its own delivery headers
records.infraweave: Adds `X-Infraweave-Delivery` and `X-Infraweave-Event` to every HTTP delivery
records.why: Receivers can deduplicate and route without parsing the body
records.impact: None; receivers may use them

records.spacelift: `retryOnFailure` retries `5xx`
records.infraweave: Also retries network errors, timeouts and `429`
records.why: A receiver that is down or throttling is a transient failure
records.impact: Receivers may see more retries and deduplicate by `X-Infraweave-Delivery`

records.spacelift: Fixed audit, notification and delivery retention
records.infraweave: Each retention is an operator setting
records.why: Storage and compliance needs are the operator's
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: Raises worker usage events for negotiated contracts
records.infraweave: Requires `events.worker_usage.limit` and `events.worker_usage.percentile`; without a limit the event is never raised
records.why: infraweave has no contracts
records.impact: Consumers of the usage event configure a limit first

records.spacelift: Selects a `Datadog` or `AWS` observability vendor
records.infraweave: OTLP is the only export; Datadog and X-Ray are reached through OTLP-capable agents
records.why: Each vendor SDK adds dependencies and code paths to test
records.impact: Operators point an OTLP collector or agent at infraweave

records.spacelift: A separate Prometheus exporter process queries the API with an API key
records.infraweave: infraweave serves the exporter's series itself at `/metrics/accounts` on the admin listener, with the `spacelift_` prefix renamed `infraweave_` and `account` and `organization` labels, the account's slug and its organization's slug, on every series
records.why: No extra process, credential or per-replica duplication; one installation hosts many organizations and accounts
records.impact: Scrape configurations target infraweave instead of the exporter, and dashboards rename the metric prefix

records.spacelift: Probes are `/readiness` and `/startup` on `:8080`
records.infraweave: Probes are `/livez`, `/readyz` and `/startupz` on `:9090`; `:8080` is the API listener
records.why: Probes stay off the public listener
records.impact: Orchestrator probe configuration changes

records.spacelift: Workers upload traces, CPU profiles and logs to a run observability bucket
records.infraweave: Workers export traces over OTLP to the operator's collector
records.why: One telemetry path, owned by the operator
records.impact: Operators run a collector the workers can reach

records.spacelift: Logs queries per request
records.infraweave: No per-request query logging at `info`; the access log records the route pattern, never the body
records.why: Bodies carry secrets and personal data
records.impact: Log pipelines that parsed query logs lose them

records.spacelift: Flows is a separately linked organization with its own login
records.infraweave: Flows belongs to the infraweave account, which takes the place of Spacelift Flows' organization: its projects, apps and agent pools are the account's, its users are the account's members, and the Deploy link is implicit
records.why: One identity and access model across the product
records.impact: No linking step; Flows users are the members the account admits

records.spacelift: HTTP Endpoint and MCP surfaces use subdomains (`mcp.`, `oauth.`)
records.infraweave: Endpoint addresses fall back to paths when no wildcard domain is configured; MCP is served at `/flows/mcp`
records.why: A self-hosted install may have no wildcard DNS
records.impact: Clients configured with Spacelift's subdomains use the paths

records.spacelift: A GraphQL Request Deploy block
records.infraweave: An API Request block over the REST API
records.why: infraweave serves no GraphQL (DV-001)
records.impact: Flows using the GraphQL block are rewritten to the API Request block

records.spacelift: Self-hosted Flows runs on EKS only
records.infraweave: Flows runs wherever infraweave runs; agents run in Kubernetes or Docker
records.why: Every reference deployment carries Flows
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: `flowctl` and `terraform-provider-flows` call RPC-style `/cli/...` and `/provider/...` routes
records.infraweave: The Flows API is REST under `/flows/v1/`; infraweave's CLI and provider replace both clients
records.why: Decision 0001's REST rule applies to every family
records.impact: `flowctl` and `terraform-provider-flows` do not work; their operations remain the parity list

records.spacelift: Intent's `discover`, `query` and `mutate` tools work over GraphQL
records.infraweave: They work over infraweave's OpenAPI operations
records.why: infraweave serves no GraphQL (DV-001)
records.impact: MCP clients see OpenAPI operation names in tool results

records.spacelift: The provided AI integration is Spacelift's, flagged `isSpaceliftProvided`, with a budget on the Free tier
records.infraweave: The provided integration is the operator's, flagged `isInstallationProvided`. Its budget is the `ai-budget` limit of each organization's tier, pooled across its accounts and metered in US dollars per 30 days from the operator's model prices; a request beyond it answers `403` `limit-reached`
records.why: The installation, not Spacelift, pays for the model, and a tier limit gives callers one refusal for every limit
records.impact: Clients read `isInstallationProvided`; operators price the default model and set `ai-budget` per tier or grant

records.spacelift: The chat transport is unpublished
records.infraweave: An infraweave-defined SSE endpoint
records.why: A transport is needed and none is documented
records.impact: Chat clients use infraweave's endpoint

records.spacelift: Spacelift's terms and documentation search
records.infraweave: The terms are the operator's, and `search_docs` searches infraweave's documentation
records.why: infraweave cannot accept terms or search docs on Spacelift's behalf
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: `spacelift-intent` does not verify provider checksums or signatures
records.infraweave: Intent verifies provider checksums and signatures
records.why: Providers run with cloud credentials on workers
records.impact: An unsigned or mismatched provider is refused

records.spacelift: Ships ECS and CloudFormation reference deployments
records.infraweave: No ECS or CloudFormation reference deployment
records.why: The supported set stays testable
records.impact: ECS operators adapt the container image themselves

records.spacelift: Infrastructure modules and the Helm chart version separately from the application
records.infraweave: Modules and chart share the application's version
records.why: One version answers which artefacts fit together
records.impact: Operators pin one version

records.spacelift: Launchers download from Spacelift and are verified with GPG keys from a public key server
records.infraweave: Launchers download from the installation itself and are verified with Sigstore
records.why: Air-gapped installs reach nothing else; no second trust root
records.impact: Worker bootstrap scripts change their download and verification steps

records.spacelift: Self-hosted needs a licence token and lacks the public pool and the Azure and GCP integrations
records.infraweave: No licence token; those limits are not inherited, and the public worker pool is a chart option (`publicWorkerPool.enabled`)
records.why: infraweave mirrors SaaS, not the self-hosted subset
records.impact: None

records.spacelift: `tier` answers a `BillingTier` enum value, and `tierFeatures` lists `BillingTierFeature` values
records.infraweave: `tier` answers a tier object: `name`, `features` (sorted infraweave feature names) and `limits` (limit name to value). `tierFeatures` answers the entitlement of the account's organization as infraweave feature names. Every operation names its capability in `x-infraweave-feature`; a switched-off feature answers `403` `feature-disabled`, and with billing on a feature outside the entitlement answers `403` `feature-not-in-tier`
records.why: Tiers are data an operator defines, which the enum cannot express, and feature names are infraweave's own
records.impact: Clients that branch on `tier` read the object's `name` or `features`; the [feature catalogue](../implementation/capability-roadmap.md#feature-catalogue) maps each `BillingTierFeature` value to its features

records.spacelift: Billing mutations change a Stripe subscription
records.infraweave: Billing mutations answer `403` `installation-unsupported`; reads answer with local meaning (`billedExternally: true`, `usage` over a trailing 30 days, empty add-on lists)
records.why: A fake success looks like progress in a test and fails in production
records.impact: Billing automation receives an explicit refusal

records.spacelift: The Azure integration, Origin and global plugin templates rely on Spacelift's own apps and catalogue
records.infraweave: They rely on operator-registered apps and catalogues: `cloud.azure`, `vcs.origin` and `plugins.catalog_paths`; without one, the operation answers `installation-unsupported`
records.why: infraweave operates no global apps
records.impact: Operators register the apps before these features work

records.spacelift: Accepts some superseded enum values in a disabled state
records.infraweave: A superseded enum value is rejected outright
records.why: A request that would do nothing should fail visibly
records.impact: Clients sending a superseded value receive `400` `invalid-request`

records.spacelift: spacectl picks one credential when several are set, in an order its docs and source disagree on, and stores profiles in `config.json` or a file per alias
records.infraweave: `infraweavectl` errors when two methods are set without `INFRAWEAVE_API_PREFERRED_METHOD`, and stores profiles in one strict YAML file, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/infraweave/config.yaml`, written `0600`
records.why: Never pick silently between conflicting inputs; one strict file
records.impact: Scripts set one credential method or the preference variable

records.spacelift: GraphQL `errors` with message text; no documented status codes or stable codes ([report 06](../research/reference/06-spacectl-and-clients.md#24-error-behaviour))
records.infraweave: An HTTP status per failure class and `application/problem+json` from one slug registry; fixed titles keep `not found` and `unauthorized` as the provider and spacectl match them; hidden and missing resources both answer `404`; field errors carry `errors` with `pointer` and `reason`; protocol endpoints answer what their own clients expect
records.why: Any HTTP client, proxy and retry library can act on the status; ported string matches keep working
records.impact: A port changes transport only; its message-text checks still match

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: Updates are whole-input mutations (`stackUpdate`, `stackConfigAdd`)
records.infraweave: Every update route keeps `PUT`, which replaces, and gains `PATCH` with `application/merge-patch+json`, in which `null` resets a field to its default; configuration elements get an item `PUT` that answers `201` or `200`
records.why: Providers want full replacement, people want to change one field
records.impact: Providers use `PUT`; CLIs and scripts may use `PATCH`

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: Last write wins
records.infraweave: Item `GET`, `PUT` and `PATCH` return a strong `ETag`; `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` accept `If-Match`, and a stale tag answers `412` `precondition-failed`. Without `If-Match`, last write wins
records.why: Optional protection against lost updates
records.impact: None unless the client sends `If-Match`

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: An unset relation reads as `null`
records.infraweave: A sub-read of an unset optional relation answers `204 No Content`
records.why: `404` on such a route always means the parent is missing or hidden
records.impact: Clients treat `204` as "none"

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: Unknown input fields are not documented as rejected
records.infraweave: Request bodies are strict: an unknown field answers `400` `invalid-request` with reason `unknown-field`; `StackInput.administrative` stays, deprecated and ignored
records.why: A misspelt body field silently ignored writes the wrong state
records.impact: Clients that send extra fields remove them

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: Label limits are undocumented
records.infraweave: Labels are 1 to 255 characters of UTF-8 with no control characters or edge whitespace, at most 100 per entity, compared byte for byte; a duplicate answers `422` `validation-failed`
records.why: Bounded, unambiguous labels
records.impact: Imports with longer, more numerous or duplicate labels fail with the field named

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: Cron and timezone acceptance is unverified
records.infraweave: Five-field cron with `*`, `n`, `a-b` and `/step`, Vixie day matching; names, `?`, `L`, `W`, `#` and `@` macros are rejected. Timezones are IANA names (embedded `time/tzdata`), absent means `UTC`; abbreviations and numeric offsets are rejected
records.why: Schedules must fire when the user expects, or fail loudly
records.impact: Imports with an expression or zone outside these rules fail with a pointer to the field

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.spacelift: Unknown keys in `.spacelift/config.yml` are unverified
records.infraweave: Known keys are typed strictly and fail the run in `INITIALIZING`; unknown keys warn in the run log and `Run.runtimeConfig`, or fail with `runs.runtime_config.unknown_keys: reject`
records.why: Failing every stack because a key is newer than infraweave turns schema lag into an outage
records.impact: Repositories with a mistyped known key see the run fail with the key's path

pending.settles: Whether Spacelift has stable error codes or is looser than infraweave's input rules

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: The worker list has no state for a worker that holds a run but has stopped polling
records.infraweave: A worker unseen for `worker.offline_after` (default 3 minutes) is an offline worker, listed with status `OFFLINE`, a fourth `WorkerStatus`, and claims no new run; its run keeps its state and stack lock until DV-025 applies
records.why: An operator needs to see which worker a waiting run depends on
records.impact: Clients that switch on `WorkerStatus` handle `OFFLINE`

records.group: Runs, workers and policies: decisions 0008 and 0009
records.spacelift: The documented worker pool setup generates an RSA 4096 key ([report 10](../research/reference/10-workers-and-execution.md#23-credentials))
records.infraweave: The pool key must be EC P-256; a CSR with any other key answers `422` `validation-failed`. Run secrets are sealed to it with infraweave's own envelope (ECDH P-256, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM)
records.why: The envelope runs under Go's FIPS 140-3 mode, and one key per pool serves both registration and sealing
records.impact: Pool setup scripts generate a P-256 key in place of RSA

records.spacelift: Terraform's and OpenTofu's `http` clients send `Content-MD5`, which a backend checks
records.infraweave: `Content-MD5` is checked as usual, except under `GODEBUG=fips140=only`, where Go refuses MD5: the header is accepted and ignored, and the body's SHA-256 is recorded and checked instead
records.why: FIPS 140-3 mode must run without an MD5 exemption, and the SHA-256 that every write records already detects a corrupt body
records.impact: None for Terraform and OpenTofu; under `fips140=only` a bad `Content-MD5` no longer answers `400`

records.spacelift: Clients poll for run logs, run state and worker pool queues
records.infraweave: Run logs, run state, worker pool queues and Flows events are also served as server-sent-event streams in the public API, each with a polling equivalent; the console's live views use them
records.why: Live views without a request per second per viewer, for the console, `infraweavectl` and integrators
records.impact: None; polling still works, and a client may switch to the streams

records.spacelift: Flows reaches Deploy through a separately linked integration
records.infraweave: Deploy events are Flows events natively, in one event model; the event kinds include drift, policy outcomes, notifications and worker changes
records.why: A run state change or a drift result triggers a flow without a bridge
records.impact: None for Deploy clients; flows that reacted to Spacelift Deploy use the Deploy trigger blocks

records.spacelift: Notification policies return strings with `spacelift::logs::*` placeholders
records.infraweave: Strings a notification policy returns are text templates ([0024](../research/decisions/0024-expression-language.md)), and `logs(phase)` replaces the placeholders
records.why: One template form across Deploy and Flows
records.impact: Notification policies that used the placeholders call `logs(phase)`

records.spacelift: Flows apps are JavaScript bundles written against `@slflows/sdk/v1` and run by agents in Node.js runtimes
records.infraweave: An app version is a multi-architecture OCI image whose program serves the versioned `App` gRPC contract; `infraweave flows-agent` runs each app in its own container. infraweave has no JavaScript runtime and no compatibility layer, and refuses a JavaScript bundle with `422` `validation-failed`
records.why: A protobuf contract evolves safely across releases, any gRPC language can serve it, and apps get ordinary libraries and networking
records.impact: Spacelift's apps and app registries do not work; an app is rebuilt as an image, in Go on `pkg/flows/appsdk` or in any gRPC language

records.spacelift: Apps may ship browser code (`ui.js`, `uiCode`)
records.infraweave: Apps contribute declarative widgets only, of fixed types the console renders
records.why: No third-party script runs in the console's origin under the user's session
records.impact: Apps that drew their own interface declare widgets instead

records.spacelift: Ships a Flows runtime image in which agents run every app
records.infraweave: No runtime image: each first-party Flows app is an OCI image of its own per app version, a Go program on `pkg/flows/appsdk`, signed and listed in infraweave's first-party app registry
records.why: Apps carry their own dependencies, and an app upgrades without an infraweave release
records.impact: Air-gapped installs mirror the app images they use into their own registry

records.spacelift: Each account's plan gates its features
records.infraweave: `billing` is a feature of the installation, off by default: no entitlement check runs and every organization behaves as Enterprise. Tiers, organization tiers and grants are data managed through the operator API (`api/operator.openapi.yaml`) and `infraweavectl operator`, effective without a restart; five tiers (Free, Starter, Starter+, Business, Enterprise) are seeded from Spacelift's documented plans
records.why: Most installations serve one company and want every feature; one that hosts others turns billing on and gets Spacelift's packaging without writing it
records.impact: None while billing is off; with billing on, organizations see Spacelift's documented gates

records.spacelift: Spacelift's names on every surface: `SPACELIFT_*` run variables, `/mnt/workspace/spacelift.oidc`, `.spacelift/` repository files, `package spacelift` policies, `spacelift_` provider resources, spacectl, `flowctl`
records.infraweave: infraweave's own names, with no Spacelift alias: `INFRAWEAVE_*` run variables such as `INFRAWEAVE_API_TOKEN` and `INFRAWEAVE_OIDC_TOKEN`, `/mnt/workspace/infraweave.oidc`, `.infraweave/config.yml` and `.infraweave/workflow.yml`, `package infraweave` with `data.infraweave.result`, `infraweave_` provider resources, and `infraweavectl`. DV-027, DV-047, DV-056 and DV-061 apply the same rule to launcher settings, check names, delivery headers and metrics
records.why: infraweave mirrors Spacelift's capabilities, not its interface; a Spacelift name would claim a compatibility infraweave does not offer
records.impact: Hooks, policies, repositories and configurations rename the prefix: `SPACELIFT_` to `INFRAWEAVE_`, `.spacelift/` to `.infraweave/`, `package spacelift` to `package infraweave`, `spacelift_` to `infraweave_`

records.spacelift: Flows expressions are JavaScript, evaluated by agents in Node.js runtimes
records.infraweave: Every expression a user writes, in Flows and in Deploy, is CEL, type-checked against its context and evaluated on the server in the `scheduler` process mode with a cost limit; agents never see an expression. Multi-step logic uses `cel.bind`, named expressions and the Transform block's steps form; there is no Script block
records.why: Expressions are bounded, deterministic and checked while the user edits, and one language serves Deploy and Flows
records.impact: Flow definitions from Spacelift import only after their expressions are rewritten in CEL

records.spacelift: `.spacelift/workflow.yml` commands are Go templates
records.infraweave: `.infraweave/workflow.yml` commands are text templates (`${{ … }}`) rendered by the runner, with every interpolated value quoted for the shell
records.why: A target or workspace name can never become shell syntax
records.impact: Custom workflow files are rewritten in the text-template form

records.spacelift: Environment variable values interpolate `${NAME}`
records.infraweave: Interpolation is `${{ env.NAME }}`, rendered on the server; `${NAME}` is left to the shell
records.why: One template form, and no ambiguity with shell syntax
records.impact: Values that relied on `${NAME}` interpolation switch to `${{ env.NAME }}`

records.spacelift: Blueprint and template context values for time and randomness change on each render
records.infraweave: They are fixed per rendered change and stored with it, so re-rendering reproduces them
records.why: Retries and replays give the same result
records.impact: None for a single render; re-renders no longer drift

records.spacelift: A stack dependency output reference copies an output as it is
records.infraweave: An output reference may carry an expression that shapes the value
records.why: Simple reshaping needs no extra stack
records.impact: None; references without an expression behave as on Spacelift

records.spacelift: Some entities carry the actions the caller may take, and the web interface decides the rest itself
records.infraweave: Every resource the API returns carries `allowedActions`, computed by the code that enforces those actions: the caller's grants and, for a resource with a state machine such as a run, the transitions its state allows
records.why: The console shows, hides or disables controls from that list alone and never decides a permission or a transition
records.impact: An added read-only field; clients that ignore it are unaffected

records.spacelift: The account is the top level: each holds its own plan, users, identity provider and spaces, and nothing groups accounts ([report 14](../research/reference/14-spaces-rbac-and-identity.md))
records.infraweave: Root, organization, account, spaces. `root` is the installation's top node, which only operators act on and which holds nothing but organizations. An organization is a customer's agreement: its tier and grants, which every account inherits; its limits, pooled across its accounts, with account limits an organization admin may set below the pool; and its members and identity providers. An account is a separate business entity and the data boundary, as a Spacelift account is. Organization admins create and remove accounts and see usage across them through the served `Organization` tag, outside the parity surface, but read none of an account's stacks, runs, state or secrets. Nothing inherits from root or from the organization. The operator API keeps the installation-level actions: creating organizations, each with its first account, tiers, grants and the billing switch
records.why: One agreement can cover separate business entities, such as two national arms of one company, whose data must stay apart while their tier, limits and people stay shared
records.impact: None for an account's own clients, which see one account as on Spacelift; the `Organization` tag is new and no Spacelift client uses it

records.spacelift: Identity is per account: each account configures its own identity provider, MFA enforcement and users, so a person in two accounts is two users
records.infraweave: Authentication happens at the organization: its identity providers, one or more, its MFA enforcement and its session lifetime. A person is one member of the organization, with roles per account; a role in one account grants nothing in another. Authorization happens per account: the account's `LOGIN` policies, evaluated on its top space, decide access and roles when the member enters it, and a member no account admits sees an empty account switcher. A session or API key works in one account at a time, API keys belong to an account, and organization keys reach only the `Organization` tag. A member counts once against `seats`; identities from two identity providers are two members until an organization admin links them, explicitly and after one sign-in through each provider, into one member ID, and nothing is linked by e-mail address
records.why: One sign-in for every account of one agreement, and one seat per person; linking by e-mail would let whoever controls an address at one provider take over a member
records.impact: SSO, SCIM and MFA settings configure the organization's identity, so a change applies to every account of the organization; scripts that manage users per account manage the account's role bindings instead

records.spacelift: A "root admin" is `space-admin` on the `root` space, and settings name "non-root admins" (`accountToggleAllowNonRootAdminSpaceCreation`, `/account/api-key-non-root-managers`); Spacelift Flows has its own "organization admin"
records.infraweave: The account admin is `space-admin` on the account's top space, which the account's immutable slug addresses. Served names say "admin" and "non-admin": `allowNonAdminSpaceCreation`, `accountToggleAllowNonAdminSpaceCreation`, `apiKeyEnableNonAdminManagers` at `/account/api-key-non-admin-managers`, and `apiKeysManagedByNonAdmins`. Spacelift Flows' organization admin is the account admin too. No served space or name is `root`, which names only the installation's top node
records.why: `root` is the installation's, and no account reaches it
records.impact: Ports address the top space by the account's slug, bind admins there, and call the renamed operations

records.spacelift: `moduleShare` shares a module with any other Spacelift account
records.infraweave: A share is the one exception to account isolation, and works only between accounts of the same organization; a share to an account of another organization answers `422` `validation-failed`. It exposes the module's fields and version downloads only, needs `module-sharing` in both accounts' entitlement, and its revocation hides the module while runs in flight finish
records.why: The organization is the agreement boundary, and accounts of different customers never see each other
records.impact: Shares to accounts outside the organization are refused

records.spacelift: `/mcp` clients authorize through Spacelift's OAuth discovery, client registration, authorization and token endpoints, whose details beyond the consent page and the redirect hosts are undocumented ([report 22](../research/reference/22-intelligence.md)); Spacelift Flows authorizes on an `oauth.` subdomain
records.infraweave: A minimal built-in OAuth authorization server for `/mcp` and `/flows/mcp`: RFC 8414 metadata, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, and authorization and token endpoints; PKCE with `S256` only; a consent page in the console, on the console session; access tokens lasting about an hour, with rotating refresh tokens; `mcp:read` and `mcp:write` scopes, narrowed by the member's normal permissions; redirect URIs limited to loopback plus the allowlist that account admins maintain
records.why: A self-hosted installation has no external authorization server, and each rule is a stated default where Spacelift's are unpublished
records.impact: MCP clients register and authorize as with any OAuth server; a client that sends `plain` PKCE or an unlisted redirect URI is refused

records.spacelift: Served API names carry Spacelift's brand: `spaceliftIntelligenceEnabled`, `accountSetSpaceliftIntelligenceEnabled`, `spaceliftIntelligenceTermsAccepted`, `spaceliftIntelligenceTermsLatestVersion`, `spaceliftAwsAccountId`, the VCS provider `SPACELIFT`, the `SpaceliftMetrics` schema and the policy input `spacelift.*`
records.infraweave: No served operationId, schema, property, enum value, header, environment variable, policy input key or description contains "spacelift". One rename table in decision 0001 maps each reference name to its infraweave name: `aiEnabled`, `accountSetAiEnabled`, `aiTermsAccepted`, `aiTermsLatestVersion`, `installationAwsAccountId`, `INFRAWEAVE`, `AccountMetrics`, `INFRAWEAVE_*` and `infraweave.*`, with DV-111's admin names. `TestUnitServedNames` checks every served bundle against the rule and the table
records.why: DV-102's rule applied to the API itself: a Spacelift name would claim a compatibility infraweave does not offer, and one table keeps every rename findable
records.impact: Ports rename these operations, fields, enum values and policy input keys as the table lists; `specref parity` treats each rename as a recorded divergence
